bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42481546 (gnutls): Global-buffer-overflow READ 8 found by fuzz target gnutls_pkcs12_key_parser_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42481546
bug_description.normalized: The staged 1011-byte PKCS#12 witness reaches `gnutls_x509_privkey_import_pkcs8()` through `gnutls_pkcs12_simple_parse()`, and its GOST `privateKeyAlgorithm.parameters.publicKeyParamSet` is parsed into one of the 256-bit GOST enums that vulnerable `get_supported_gost_curve()` aliases to the local `nettle_get_gost_256cpa()` backport (`GNUTLS_ECC_CURVE_GOST256CPA`, `GNUTLS_ECC_CURVE_GOST256CPXA`, or `GNUTLS_ECC_CURVE_GOST256B`). Import fixup then passes that local backport curve object into the externally linked Nettle library for `ecc_point_mul_g()`. GnuTLS's local backport was compiled with a different `struct ecc_curve` tail layout than the linked Nettle sources, so external `ecc_point_mul_g()` interprets the local `unit` pointer as `pippenger_table`. `ecc_mul_g()` therefore calls `sec_tabselect()` on the 32-byte global `ecc_unit` object as if it were the full precomputed generator table, and `sec_tabselect()` reads 8 bytes into the redzone immediately before `ecc_table`. The saved ASan stack `_nettle_sec_tabselect -> _nettle_ecc_mul_g -> nettle_ecc_point_mul_g -> wrap_nettle_pk_fixup -> gnutls_x509_privkey_import_pkcs8 -> gnutls_pkcs12_simple_parse` and the reported globals from `gost/ecc-gost256cpa-64.h` match this chain.

source.description: First project statement on the witnessed path that reads the attacker-controlled GOST curve OID from the PKCS#8 parameters into a parser buffer.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is a DER PKCS#12 blob. After `gnutls_pkcs12_simple_parse()` extracts a key bag and dispatches it into `gnutls_x509_privkey_import_pkcs8()`, `_decode_pkcs8_gost_key()` reads `privateKeyAlgorithm.parameters` and passes that DER blob to `_gnutls_x509_read_gost_params()`. This line materializes the witness-controlled `publicKeyParamSet` OID into `oid`; step 2 converts it into one of the 256-bit GOST enums that vulnerable `get_supported_gost_curve()` aliases to `nettle_get_gost_256cpa()`.

sink.description: ASan crash site. `sec_tabselect()` reads limbs from a base pointer derived from the wrong `struct ecc_curve` field, so the 8-byte load crosses from the 32-byte `ecc_unit` object into the redzone before `ecc_table`.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `READ of size 8` here, at an address 0 bytes to the right of global `ecc_unit` and 32 bytes to the left of global `ecc_table` in `gost/ecc-gost256cpa-64.h`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. Vulnerable `get_supported_gost_curve()` aliases `GNUTLS_ECC_CURVE_GOST256CPA`, `GNUTLS_ECC_CURVE_GOST256CPXA`, and `GNUTLS_ECC_CURVE_GOST256B` to the locally-built legacy `nettle_get_gost_256cpa()` backport. That local object is later consumed by external Nettle with an incompatible `struct ecc_curve` layout.
root_cause.note: The staged patch adds a `NEED_GOSTDSA` capability check, renames the local curve accessors and objects to GC256B/GC512A names, and rewrites `get_supported_gost_curve()` so `GOST256CPA`, `GOST256CPXA`, and `GOST256B` all resolve via the `GOST256B` fallthrough to `nettle_get_gost_gc256b()`, while `GOST512A` resolves to `nettle_get_gost_gc512a()`. It also moves the local-only VKO and unmask declarations into `gostdsa2.h`, so this path no longer returns the old local `_gnutls_gost_256cpa` or `_gnutls_gost_512a` objects.

tainted_value_origin.description: The attacker-chosen GOST parameter-set OID becomes the imported key's `params->curve` here. That enum later drives the vulnerable `get_supported_gost_curve()` switch.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: Step 2 resolves the witness-controlled `publicKeyParamSet` OID to one of the 256-bit GOST enums that vulnerable `get_supported_gost_curve()` aliases to `nettle_get_gost_256cpa()` (`GNUTLS_ECC_CURVE_GOST256CPA`, `GNUTLS_ECC_CURVE_GOST256CPXA`, or `GNUTLS_ECC_CURVE_GOST256B`), and this assignment commits that enum into the imported key parameters.

parser_admitted.code: ret = gnutls_x509_privkey_import_pkcs8(*key, &data, GNUTLS_X509_FMT_DER, password, type == GNUTLS_BAG_PKCS8_KEY ? GNUTLS_PKCS_PLAIN : 0);
parser_admitted.description: By this point the PKCS#12 blob has been imported successfully, a key bag has been extracted, and its PKCS#8 bytes are dispatched into the private-key importer with the harness password `"1234"`, admitting the witness to the vulnerable GOST key path.

coarse_trace.summary: A key bag from the attacker-controlled PKCS#12 blob is routed into `gnutls_x509_privkey_import_pkcs8()`.

The GOST parameter parser reads `publicKeyParamSet`, converts it to one of the supported 256-bit GOST enums that vulnerable fixup later aliases to `nettle_get_gost_256cpa()`, and stores that enum in the imported key parameters.

Import fixup asks `get_supported_gost_curve()` for that enum, and the vulnerable switch aliases `GOST256CPA`, `GOST256CPXA`, and `GOST256B` to the local legacy `nettle_get_gost_256cpa()` curve object before binding that pointer into Nettle point and scalar state.
External Nettle interprets the local curve object with its own `struct ecc_curve` layout, so the generator-table field resolves to `ecc_unit` instead of `ecc_table`.
The selection loop reads past the 32-byte `ecc_unit` object into the redzone before `ecc_table`, producing the saved global-buffer-overflow.

fine_trace.note: Source. The PKCS#8 GOST parameter parser reads the witness-controlled `publicKeyParamSet` OID string out of the imported ASN.1 object and stores it in `oid` for curve dispatch.

The parsed OID is converted into the internal curve enum. Because the saved crash later dereferences globals from `gost/ecc-gost256cpa-64.h` and vulnerable `get_supported_gost_curve()` only returns that local object for `GNUTLS_ECC_CURVE_GOST256CPA`, `GNUTLS_ECC_CURVE_GOST256CPXA`, or `GNUTLS_ECC_CURVE_GOST256B`, the witness reaches one of those three enums here; the staged artifacts do not disambiguate further.

The imported GOST private-key parameters retain that attacker-chosen 256-bit GOST enum for later fixup. Reaching this assignment also means the `if (curve == GNUTLS_ECC_CURVE_INVALID)` cleanup path was not taken, so `params->curve` now carries one of the three values identified in step 2.

Root cause. When `wrap_nettle_pk_fixup()` asks for the GOST curve implementation, this switch aliases `GNUTLS_ECC_CURVE_GOST256CPA`, `GNUTLS_ECC_CURVE_GOST256CPXA`, and `GNUTLS_ECC_CURVE_GOST256B` to the locally-built legacy `nettle_get_gost_256cpa()` object instead of the GC256B object that matches external Nettle's layout. The saved crash proves the witness reaches this alias set, but the staged artifacts do not pin it to one enum inside the set.
The selected local curve pointer from step 4 is bound into the imported private scalar object, so later scalar multiplication will assert against and use that same curve object.
During `wrap_nettle_pk_fixup()`'s `ecc_point_init(&r, curve)` call, the same local curve pointer is stored in `r.ecc` for generator multiplication.

External Nettle now interprets `r->ecc` and `n->ecc` using its own `struct ecc_curve` definition from `nettle/ecc-internal.h`, where `unit` and `pippenger_table` follow `b`. But the object returned in step 4 came from GnuTLS's local backport (`gnutls/lib/nettle/gost/ecc-gost256cpa.c`) built against `gnutls/lib/nettle/gost/ecc-internal.h`, which inserts an extra `g` field before `unit`. Under the external layout, `ecc->pippenger_table` therefore resolves to the local `ecc_unit` pointer instead of `ecc_table`.

With the misread `ecc->pippenger_table` from step 7 and the first Pippenger row (`j == 0`), this call hands `sec_tabselect()` a base pointer to the 32-byte `ecc_unit` object while still declaring each row to be `2 * ecc->p.size` limbs wide.

Sink. `sec_tabselect()` iterates over that bogus table base and reads 8-byte limbs from `p == ecc_unit`; after the 32-byte `ecc_unit` object is exhausted, the next load falls into the global redzone immediately before `ecc_table`, exactly as reported by ASan.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch first checks whether the linked Nettle already provides `nettle_get_gost_gc256b()` / `nettle_get_gost_gc512a()` and the needed GOST DSA helpers; only when they are missing does GnuTLS build the renamed local backports and keep the local-only VKO and unmask declarations in `gostdsa2.h`. In `get_supported_gost_curve()`, it removes the separate `GOST256CPA` and `GOST256CPXA` returns so those cases fall through with `GOST256B` to `nettle_get_gost_gc256b()`, and it rewrites `GOST512A` to `nettle_get_gost_gc512a()`. That eliminates the old `_gnutls_gost_256cpa` / `_gnutls_gost_512a` objects from this call path and aligns the curve object layout with the linked Nettle implementation.

format.name: DER-encoded PKCS#12 blob consumed by gnutls_pkcs12_key_parser_fuzzer
format.contract: The verified witness is the exact staged 1011-byte DER PKCS#12 blob at `gt_results/arvo_42481546/poc`. It must import far enough for `gnutls_pkcs12_simple_parse()` to extract a PKCS#8 GOST private-key bag and call `gnutls_x509_privkey_import_pkcs8()` with the harness password `"1234"`. Inside that PKCS#8, `privateKeyAlgorithm.parameters.publicKeyParamSet` must decode to one of the 256-bit GOST curve enums that vulnerable `get_supported_gost_curve()` aliases to the local `nettle_get_gost_256cpa()` object (`GNUTLS_ECC_CURVE_GOST256CPA`, `GNUTLS_ECC_CURVE_GOST256CPXA`, or `GNUTLS_ECC_CURVE_GOST256B`). The staged artifacts do not prove which of those three the witness carries, only that it reaches this aliased `nettle_get_gost_256cpa()` import-fixup path. This contract is limited to the exact staged witness and observed local-256cpa crash path, not all PKCS#12 or GOST inputs.
